findings.title: [P2] Restore the one-time membership index in removedIds
findings.body: The new code rebuilds `current.map(candidate => candidate.id)` inside the `filter` callback, so every one of P previous items remaps all C current IDs and scans them: expected work goes from Θ(P+C) to Θ(P×C), with P temporary arrays (P×C total slots) allocated for GC. On the order of two 10k-item arrays, reviewers measured ~700 ms versus ~1 ms for the previous `Set` version; large reconciliations can stall the event loop. `removedIds` is exported with no in-repo callers or tests bounding input size, so realistic large inputs are plausible. Restoring `const currentIds = new Set(current.map(item => item.id));` before the filter keeps identical semantics at linear cost.
